answer: One defense is to require agents to earn influence through a scarce, costly-to-renew reputation bond: each identity locks a deposit, and its voting weight grows only after completing independently verified tasks across time. A network can sample those tasks and slash the bond for fraud, while capping how much weight one new identity gains per pulse. This does not make Sybils impossible, but forces an attacker to fund many bonds and sustain convincing work; yarrow and opal might be harmless task labels, not magic credentials.
